## §7.1.1: The Anthropomorphic Pivot &amp; Cognitive Pluralism {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">OPENING OF TEIL B &amp; STRATUM D (SM, PP. 122–123) | CLAIM CEILING: (D, R, Explicatum, S₀, E₂)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.intuition-box}
**Historical Vignette: Number Fields and Measurement (§7.1):**
The historical dialogue between structural and operational approaches to physics is useful as motivation only. The quantitative layer is defined by explicit algebraic types and measurement maps rather than by biographical authority.
:::

* Chapters 1–6 completed **Teil A**: universal categorical logic, operadic synthesis, corporate networks, gauge curvature, higher Metroplex towers, and telecentric attractors—yet purely qualitative and devoid of numerical coordinates or laboratory units.
* In §7.1 of SM (pp. 122–123), Heim executes the **Anthropomorphic Pivot** by analyzing the concrete cognitive architecture of the human observer (*normal-psychische Konstellation*):
  * **Bivalent Baseline ($A_0$):** Elementary two-valued contradictory predication (*zweiwertige, kontradiktorische Prädikation*) sorts raw stimuli into affirmation ($\overline{|\Pi|}_+$) and negation ($\overline{|\Pi|}_-$), normalized by $\sum h_i = 1$.
  * **Cognitive Pluralism:** Every moment of awareness engages a simultaneous plurality of subjective aspects:
    $$
    S_{\mathrm{human}} = \bigcup_{i \in I} S_i
    $$

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-right}
***Qualität* (Regional Pluralism) vs. *Quantität* (Global Unification):**

1. **Qualität (*Apodiktische Pluralitäten*, SM p. 123):** Color qualia, timbre, affective valence, and ethical norms differ in intrinsic kind rather than scalar magnitude; in $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{iMSL}}$, propositions achieve necessity ($\Box_S$) only across localized sub-regions.
2. **Quantität (*Mengendialektik*):** Spatial extension, duration, mass, and counts admit equality ($\overline{|m|}_+ \equiv {=}$) vs. strict ordering ($\overline{|m|}_- \equiv {\neq} \implies a > b \lor a < b$), converging onto the single overarching **$\quantitaetsaspekt$** via Friedman (2001) &amp; van Fraassen (2008) coordinative definitions over $\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}$.
:::

## §7.1.2: The *Quantitätssyntrix* (SM-28) &amp; *Synkolationsfelder* {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-d">STRATUM D: QUANTITÄTSSYNTRIX (SM, PP. 124–130, EQ. 28) &amp; LAYERED STRUKTURKASKADEN</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**The *Quantitätssyntrix* ($\quantitaetssyntrix$) &amp; Historical Schema (SM Eq. 28, p. 127):**
1. **Apodictic Idea of Quantity ($\zahlenkoerper$):** Realized through algebraic number fields $\mathbb{Q}, \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}$ with quantity increase ($+, \cdot$) and decrease ($-, :$) (SM, p. 124).
2. **Metrophor Types for $\quantitaetssyntrix$:**
   * *Singularer Metrophor* ($\widetilde{a} = (a_i)_q$): Pure dimensionless constants (SM, p. 125).
   * *Semantischer Metrophor* ($R_n = (y_l)_n$): $n$-dimensional parameter continuum ($0 \le y_l \le \infty$) of dimensioned physical magnitudes (SM, p. 126).
   * *Semantischer Iterator* ($S_n$): Clothes pure numbers with physical dimensions:
     $$
     \mathrm{S}_n ; \tilde{\mathrm{a}} = \mathrm{R}_n, \quad \tilde{\mathrm{a}} = (\mathrm{a}_i)_q, \quad \tilde{\mathrm{a}}| = \langle \mathrm{f}, \mathrm{R}_n, \mathrm{m} \rangle \tag{SM-28}
     $$
3. **Action of *Funktionaloperator* ($f$) &amp; *Synkolationsfelder* (${}^m\bar{A}$):** Selects $m$ coordinates $R_m \subseteq R_n$ in $\binom{n}{m}$ distinct ways to generate a rank-$k$ tensor field within the $(m + m^k)$-dimensional **Synkolatorraum**, distinguishing unoriented scalars ($\bar{a}\cdot\bar{b}$) from oriented tensors ($\bar{a}\times\bar{b}$), organized by **Feldzentren** (critical extrema, p. 129) and **Isoklinen** (level contours, p. 130).
:::

::: {.firewall-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Architectural Principle of Layered *Strukturkaskaden* (SM, p. 130):**
> *"Entscheidend ist, daß nur der Synkolator des ersten Syndroms die Feldbereiche direkt aus $R_n$ induziert, während höhere Synkolatoren die Tensorfelder aus der Besetzung des vorangegangenen Syndroms verarbeiten."*

$$
R_n \xrightarrow{\;f_1\;} F_1({}^m\bar{A}_1) \xrightarrow{\;f_2\;} F_2({}^m\bar{A}_2) \xrightarrow{\;f_3\;} \dots \xrightarrow{\;f_M\;} F_M({}^m\bar{A}_M)
$$
:::

## §7.2.1: Coefficient Poset $\Coeff$ &amp; Realification Functor $V_{\mathbb{R}}$ {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: SCHOLIUM 7.1, CARNAP 7.1, DEFINITION 7.2 &amp; REALIFICATION BUNDLE (FIGS. 7.1–7.2) | STAGE S₂</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.scholium-box}
**Scholium 7.1 (Number Field Posets &amp; Realification Functors) &amp; Index Conventions:**
1. **Categorical Typing:** $\Coeff \coloneqq [\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R} \subseteq \mathbb{C}]$ types discrete counts ($\mathbb{Q}$), continua ($\mathbb{R}$), and quantum phase amplitudes ($\mathbb{C}$) with functorial scalar extensions.
2. **Normed Carrier Realification:** $(V)_{\mathbb{R}}$ equips spaces over $\mathbb{K}$ with canonical real Banach norms: $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}((\mathbb{C}^n)_{\mathbb{R}}) = 2n$, $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}((\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathbb{R}}) = n$.
3. **Chapter 7 Indices:** $\mathbb{K} \in \{\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$; Metrophor rank $n \in \mathbb{N}$; real dimension factor $d(\mathbb{K}) \in \{1,2\}$; active submanifold $m \le n$; tensor rank $k \in \mathbb{N}_0$; chart output $d \le m$; operadic arity $r \in \mathbb{N}$.
:::

::: {.carnap-box .fragment .fade-right}
**Carnap 7.1 (Dimensional Parameter Functors as Coordinative Definitions):**
In *Testability and Meaning* (1936/37) and *Methodological Character of Theoretical Concepts* (1956), Carnap showed that theoretical terms ($L_T$) gain empirical meaning via reduction sentences to observational language ($L_O$). Following Friedman (2001) and van Fraassen (2008), the **Realification Functor** $(V)_{\mathbb{R}}$ and **Dimensional Parameter Functor** $S_n \colon \DimField \to \mathbf{Ban}_{\le 1}$ execute this exact coordinative bridge from dimensionless tuples $(\mathbb{K}^q)_{\mathbb{R}}$ to normed parameter continua $R_n$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 7.2 (The Category $\Coeff$ of Coefficient Field Adjunctions):**
$\Coeff = [\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R} \subseteq \mathbb{C}]$ is a finite total order and complete lattice under binary meets $\mathbb{K} \wedge \mathbb{L} \coloneqq \mathbb{K} \cap \mathbb{L} = \min(\mathbb{K}, \mathbb{L})$. For a $\mathbb{K}$-vector space $V$, its **Realification** is:
$$
V_{\mathbb{R}} \coloneqq \begin{cases} \mathbb{R} \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} V & \mathbb{K} = \mathbb{Q}, \\ V & \mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}, \\ \operatorname{Res}_{\mathbb{R}}^{\mathbb{C}}(V) & \mathbb{K} = \mathbb{C}, \end{cases} \qquad d(\mathbb{Q})=1,\; d(\mathbb{R})=1,\; d(\mathbb{C})=2
$$
with $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}((\mathbb{K}^n)_{\mathbb{R}}) = d(\mathbb{K})n$ and isometric $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra representation $\rho_{\mathbb{K}} \colon \mathbb{K} \to \mathcal{L}(V_{\mathbb{R}})$ satisfying $\rho_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathrm{i}) = J_{\mathbb{C}}$, $J_{\mathbb{C}}^2 = -\operatorname{id}$, and $\|J_{\mathbb{C}}\|_{\mathrm{op}} = 1$.
:::

## §7.2.1: Quantitative Contexts $\Ctxquant$ &amp; Pullback Completeness {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A/B: DEFINITIONS 7.3–7.4 &amp; PROPOSITION 7.5 PROOF | FORMALIZATION STAGE S₁b / S₂</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 7.3 (Category $\Ctxquant$) &amp; Definition 7.4 (Realization Functor $U_{\mathrm{quant}}$):**
* **Objects $U_Q \coloneqq (U, n_U, \mathbb{K}_U, \rho_U)$:** $U \in \operatorname{Obj}(\mathbf{Ctx}_{\mathrm{adm}}^{\mathrm{sk}})$, field $\mathbb{K}_U \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Coeff)$, and norm-preserving $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra representation $\rho_U \colon \mathbb{K}_U \to \mathcal{L}(P^U)$ equipping the Predicatrix carrier:
  $$
  U_{\mathrm{quant}}(U_Q) \;\coloneqq\; P^U \;\cong\; (\mathbb{K}_U^{n_U})_{\mathbb{R}} \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{R}^3 \;\cong\; \mathbb{R}^{3 d(\mathbb{K}_U) n_U}
  $$
  such that $z^U \in \operatorname{Isom}_{\mathbb{K}_U}(P^U)$ commutes with $\rho_U(\mathbb{K}_U)$.
* **Morphisms $\alpha \colon U_Q \to V_Q$:** Context morphism $\alpha = (\alpha_D, \alpha_P, \alpha_C)$ with subfield inclusion $\iota \colon \mathbb{K}_U \hookrightarrow \mathbb{K}_V$ intertwining scalar actions and preserving cipher subspaces:
  $$
  \alpha_P \circ \rho_U(\lambda) = \rho_V(\iota(\lambda)) \circ \alpha_P \quad (\forall \lambda \in \mathbb{K}_U), \qquad z^V(\operatorname{Im}(\alpha_P)) \subseteq \operatorname{Im}(\alpha_P)
  $$
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proposition 7.5 &amp; Proof (Well-Definedness &amp; Pullback Completeness of $\Ctxquant$):**
$\Ctxquant$ is a well-defined category with all finite pullbacks, the forgetful functor $I \colon \Ctxquant \to \mathbf{Ctx}_{\mathrm{adm}}^{\mathrm{sk}}$ strictly preserves pullbacks, and $U_{\mathrm{quant}} \colon \Ctxquant \to \mathbf{Ban}_{\le 1}$ is contractive.

**Proof:** Composition intertwines via $(\beta_P\circ\alpha_P)\circ\rho_U(\lambda) = \rho_W((\iota_2\circ\iota_1)(\lambda))\circ(\beta_P\circ\alpha_P)$. Given a cospan $V_{1,Q} \xrightarrow{\alpha} U_Q \xleftarrow{\beta} V_{2,Q}$, set $\mathbb{K}_W \coloneqq \mathbb{K}_{V_1} \cap \mathbb{K}_{V_2} = \min(\mathbb{K}_{V_1}, \mathbb{K}_{V_2}) \in \Coeff$. On the pullback context $W = V_1 \times_U V_2$, define $\rho_W(\lambda)(p_1, p_2) \coloneqq (\rho_{V_1}(\lambda)p_1, \rho_{V_2}(\lambda)p_2)$ for $\lambda \in \mathbb{K}_W$. Whenever $\alpha_P(p_1) = \beta_P(p_2)$, intertwining gives $\alpha_P(\rho_{V_1}(\lambda)p_1) = \rho_U(\lambda)(\alpha_P(p_1)) = \rho_U(\lambda)(\beta_P(p_2)) = \beta_P(\rho_{V_2}(\lambda)p_2)$, so $P^W \subset P^{V_1}\oplus_\infty P^{V_2}$ is closed under $\rho_W(\mathbb{K}_W)$, yielding a universal pullback strictly preserved by $I$. $\blacksquare$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

Each quantitative coordinate $l \in \{1, \dots, n_U\}$ carries a realified $\mathbb{K}_U$-fiber $(\mathbb{K}_U)_{\mathbb{R}} \cong \mathbb{R}^{d(\mathbb{K}_U)}$ tensored with the 3-dimensional syntrometric predicate space $\mathbb{R}^3$ (affirmation, negation, and dialectical synthesis), while isometric cipher $z^U \in \operatorname{Isom}_{\mathbb{K}_U}(P^U)$ commutes with $\rho_U(\mathbb{K}_U)$.

  Because $\Coeff = [\mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{R} \subseteq \mathbb{C}]$ is a finite total order, any cospan $\mathbb{K}_{V_1} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{K}_U \hookleftarrow \mathbb{K}_{V_2}$ has an exact pullback $\mathbb{K}_W = \mathbb{K}_{V_1} \cap \mathbb{K}_{V_2} = \min(\mathbb{K}_{V_1}, \mathbb{K}_{V_2})$ on which $\rho_W = \rho_{V_1} \times \rho_{V_2}$ restricts cleanly to the fiber product $P^W \subset P^{V_1} \oplus_\infty P^{V_2}$.

## §7.2.1: Quantitative Topos $\Equant$, Geometric Morphism &amp; Dedekind Reals {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM A/B: DEFS. 7.6, 7.8 &amp; THEOREMS 7.7, 7.9 PROOFS | CLAIM CEILING: (B, M, Derivation, S₁b, E₃)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 7.6 &amp; Theorem 7.7 (Topology $\Jquant$ &amp; Geometric Morphism $\pi_{\mathrm{quant}} \colon \Equant \to \Esyn$):**
Let $I \colon \Ctxquant \to \mathbf{Ctx}_{\mathrm{adm}}^{\mathrm{sk}}$ be the pullback-preserving forgetful functor. Define $S \in \Jquant(U_Q) \iff \langle I(S)\rangle \in \Jsyn(I(U_Q))$ and $\Equant \coloneqq \mathbf{Sh}(\Ctxquant, \Jquant)$.
1. $\Jquant$ unconditionally satisfies the three Grothendieck topology axioms (maximality, pullback stability, transitivity; Mac Lane &amp; Moerdijk 1994).
2. Since $I$ is a morphism of sites, it induces a canonical **Geometric Morphism of Toposes**:
   $$
   \pi_{\mathrm{quant}} = \left(\pi_{\mathrm{quant}}^* \dashv \pi_{\mathrm{quant}*}\right) \colon \Equant \longrightarrow \Esyn
   $$
   where $(\pi_{\mathrm{quant}*}\mathbf{F})(U) = \lim_{I(U_Q)\to U}\mathbf{F}(U_Q)$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{quant}}^* = \mathbf{a}_{\Jquant}(-\circ I^{\mathrm{op}})$ is exact.

**Proof:** (1) $\operatorname{id}_{I(U_Q)} \in I(\operatorname{Max}(U_Q)) \implies \langle I(\operatorname{Max}(U_Q))\rangle \in \Jsyn$. (2) By Prop. 7.5, $I$ preserves pullbacks, so $\langle I(h^*S)\rangle = I(h)^*\langle I(S)\rangle \in \Jsyn$. (3) Transitivity follows from $\Jsyn$, and Grothendieck's site theorem (Ch. VII.10) yields $\pi_{\mathrm{quant}}^* \dashv \pi_{\mathrm{quant}*}$. $\blacksquare$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Def. 7.8 &amp; Theorem 7.9 (Internal Dedekind vs. Cauchy Reals in $\Equant$):**
* **Def. 7.8 ($\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}$):** Subobject pairs $(L, U)$ of $\mathbb{Q}_{\mathcal{E}}$ that are inhabited, downward/upward closed, rounded, disjoint ($L \cap U = \emptyset$), and **located** in Heyting logic: $\forall q < r \in \mathbb{Q}_{\mathcal{E}},\; L(q) \vee U(r)$.
* **Thm. 7.9 &amp; Proof:** $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}$ is an internal ordered ring. Each Cauchy name defines a cut via lower/upper bounds, giving a canonical monomorphism $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{Cauchy}} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}$. Reversing this map requires selecting arbitrarily small rational intervals around a located cut, so isomorphism holds under internal countable choice (or local compactness/completeness), and $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{E}}(U) \cong C^0(\mathcal{S}_P^U, \mathbb{R})$ requires additional site hypotheses rather than being automatic. $\blacksquare$
:::

## §7.2.2: Bounded Tensor Spaces &amp; Colored Operad $\Oquant$ {.smaller transition="convex"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-a">STRATUM A: DEFINITIONS 7.10–7.12 &amp; TENSOR OPERAD ACTION RIBBON (FIG. 7.3) | STAGE S₁b</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Def. 7.10 (Scalar vs. Tensorial Products) &amp; Def. 7.11 (Banach Tensor Spaces):**
* **Def. 7.10 (SM, p. 128):** In the $\quantitaetsaspekt$, the **scalar product** $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$ contracts directional data to a scalar, whereas the **tensorial product** retains directional information in a tensor-valued result (not restricted to the 3D cross product).
* **Def. 7.11 (Bounded Continuous Tensor Fields):** Over a smooth $m$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(R_m, g_m)$, let $T^{\otimes k}R_m$ be the pure contravariant rank-$k$ tensor bundle with fiberwise norm $\|\cdot\|_{g_m}$. The space:
  $$
  X_{(m,k)} \;\coloneqq\; \Gamma_b^0(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m) \;=\; \left\{ A \in \Gamma(R_m, T^{\otimes k}R_m) \;\middle|\; \|A\|_{C_b^0} \coloneqq \sup_{y \in R_m}\|A(y)\|_{g_m} < \infty \right\}
  $$
  is a real Banach space (Ryan 2002).
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 7.12 (Colored Operad $\Oquant$ &amp; Isometric Suboperad $\Oisom$):**
With colors $\mathbf{Col}_{\mathrm{tensor}} \coloneqq \{(m, k) \in \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}_0\}$, the $\mathsf{Ban}$-enriched colored operad $\Oquant$ has:
1. **Operation Spaces:** Bounded multilinear operators under the projective cross-norm $\widehat{\otimes}_\pi$:
   $$
   \Oquant\big((m_1, k_1), \dots, (m_r, k_r);\; (m, k)\big) \;\coloneqq\; \mathcal{B}\!\left(X_{(m_1, k_1)} \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi X_{(m_r, k_r)},\; X_{(m, k)}\right)
   $$
   with $\|f\|_{\mathrm{op}} \coloneqq \sup_{\|A_i\|\le 1}\|f(A_1, \dots, A_r)\|_{C_b^0}$ and identity $\operatorname{id}_{(m,k)}$.
2. **Operadic Substitution:** $\gamma(f; g_1, \dots, g_r) \coloneqq f \circ (g_1 \widehat{\otimes}_\pi \dots \widehat{\otimes}_\pi g_r)$ extends contractively via the universal property of $\widehat{\otimes}_\pi$.
3. **Isometric Natural Suboperad $\Oisom \subseteq \Oquant$:** Single-base operations equivariant under the isometry Lie group $G_m = \operatorname{Isom}(R_m, g_m)$:
   $$
   f(\varphi_* A_1, \dots, \varphi_* A_r) = \varphi_* f(A_1, \dots, A_r) \quad \forall \varphi \in G_m
   $$
:::

:::

## §7.3.1: Dimensional Parameter Functor $S_n$ &amp; Continuous Metropie Flow {.smaller transition="slide"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DERIVED CONSTRUCTIONS — DEFINITION 7.13 &amp; LIE GROUP METROPIE FLOW (FIG. 7.4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 7.13 (Category $\DimField$ and Dimensional Parameter Functor $S_n$):**
Let $\DimField$ be the category whose:
* **Objects:** Pairs $(\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda})$ where $\mathbb{K} \in \operatorname{Obj}(\Coeff)$ and $\mathbf{\Lambda} = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)$ is a positive diagonal scaling matrix ($\lambda_l > 0$ encoding physical units).
* **Morphisms:** Scale-contractive inclusions $\iota \colon (\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda}) \to (\mathbb{L}, \mathbf{\Lambda}')$ satisfying $\lambda'_l \|\iota(x)\|_{\mathbb{L}} \le \lambda_l \|x\|_{\mathbb{K}}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{K}$ ($1 \le l \le n$).
* **Dimensional Parameter Functor $S_n \colon \DimField \to \mathbf{Ban}_{\le 1}$:** Assigns to $(\mathbb{K}, \mathbf{\Lambda})$ the realified parameter space $R_n \coloneqq (\mathbb{K}^n)_{\mathbb{R}} \cong \mathbb{R}^{d(\mathbb{K})n}$ equipped with the weighted norm:
  $$
  \|y\|_{R_n} \;\coloneqq\; \max_{1 \le l \le n} \lambda_l \|y_l\|_{\mathbb{K}}
  $$
  and maps morphisms to $\widetilde{\iota} \colon R_n(\mathbb{K}) \to R_n(\mathbb{L})$ with $S_n(\operatorname{id}) = \operatorname{id}_{R_n}$ and $S_n(\iota_2 \circ \iota_1) = S_n(\iota_2) \circ S_n(\iota_1)$.
:::

::: {.intuition-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Continuous Metropie Flow on the Lie Group of Isometric Ciphers (Fig. 7.4):**
On realified carriers $P^U$, orientation-preserving isometric ciphers form the compact Lie group $\operatorname{Isom}^+(P^U) \cong \mathrm{SO}(n)$ with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(n)$. A continuous *Metropie* transition $\gamma(t) = z(t) \in \mathrm{SO}(n)$ from $z(0) = z^U$ to $z(1) = z^V$ carries the positive-definite Killing–Cartan metric tensor:
$$
g_{\mathrm{met}}(\dot{z}, \dot{z}) \coloneqq -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left((z^{-1}\dot{z}) \circ (z^{-1}\dot{z})\right) \ge 0, \qquad d_{\mathbf{Ctx}}(U, V) \le \int_0^1 \sqrt{g_{\mathrm{met}}(\dot{\gamma}, \dot{\gamma})}\,dt
$$
:::

:::

## §7.3.2: Geometry of *Synkolatorraum*: Isocline Foliations &amp; Morse–Bott Centers {.smaller transition="zoom"}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SCHOLIUM 7.14, DEFINITION 7.15, TOY EXAMPLE &amp; CORNERS FOLIATION (FIG. 7.5)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.scholium-box}
**Scholium 7.14 (Meta-Theoretic Justification: Isocline Foliations &amp; Field Centers):**
Differential topology reconstructs Heim's intuitive geometric contours (*Isoklinen*) and focal extrema (*Feldzentren*, SM pp. 129–130) with coordinate-free rigor:
1. **Regular Isoclines as Foliations:** By the constant-rank submersion theorem on $R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}$, level sets $\Sigma_c = ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c)$ are embedded submanifolds of codimension $d$ forming a regular foliation $\mathfrak{f}_A$.
2. **Feldzentren as Morse–Bott Submanifolds:** Extrema of $\Phi(A) = \|A\|_{g_m}^2$ form the critical locus $d(\Phi\circ A) = 0$, decomposing under Morse–Bott regularity into disjoint smooth critical submanifolds $\bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha$.
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Definition 7.15 (*Synkolatorraum* $\Msyn$, Submersion Foliation $\mathfrak{f}_A$ &amp; Field Centers $Z_\alpha$):**
1. **Synkolatorraum:** Total space $\Msyn \coloneqq T^{\otimes k}R_m$ with $\dim(\Msyn) = m + m^k$.
2. **Regular Locus &amp; Foliation:** For smooth component map ${}^m\bar{A} \colon R_m \to \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \le m$),
   $$
   R_m^{\mathrm{reg}} \coloneqq \big\{y \in R_m \;\big|\; \operatorname{rank}(d({}^m\bar{A})_y) = d\big\}, \qquad \Sigma_c \coloneqq ({}^m\bar{A})^{-1}(c) \cap R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}
   $$
   Connected components of $\Sigma_c$ form a smooth **codimension-$d$ foliation** $\mathfrak{f}_A$ on $R_m^{\mathrm{reg}}$.
3. **Critical Field Centers:** For $\Phi(A) \coloneqq \|A\|_{g_m}^2$, $Z(A, g_m, \Phi) \coloneqq \{y \in R_m \mid d(\Phi\circ A)_y = 0\} = \bigsqcup_\alpha Z_\alpha$ ($\dim Z_\alpha = d_\alpha \le m$).
:::

::: {.remark-box .fragment .blur-in}
**Remark (Toy Example: 2D Parameter Space with Concentric Isoclines):**
On $R_2 = \mathbb{R}^2$ ($g = \delta_{ij}$) with scalar field ($k=0$) $f(y_1, y_2) = y_1^2 + y_2^2$: $\Msyn = R_2 \times \mathbb{R}^1 \cong \mathbb{R}^3$; regular locus $R_2^{\mathrm{reg}} = \mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{(0,0)\}$ since $df = (2y_1, 2y_2) \ne (0,0)$; **Isoclines** $\Sigma_c = \{y_1^2 + y_2^2 = c\}$ ($c>0$) are concentric circles of radius $\sqrt{c}$; **Field Center** $Z = \{(0,0)\}$ (*Fehlstelle* $\mathbf{0}$ in Fig. 7.5) is an isolated 0D Morse minimum.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

## §7.3.3: Layered Processing Cascade, Initial Section $A_0$ &amp; Musical Pullbacks {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: DEFINITION 7.16, PROPOSITION 7.17 &amp; STRUKTURKASKADE PIPELINE (FIG. 7.6)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Definition 7.16 (Canonical Coordinate Frame Initial Section $A_0$):**
Let $\pi_1 \colon R_n \to R_{m_1}$ project onto the active $m_1$-dimensional subspace ($m_1 \le n$), and let $X_0 \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_1}, TR_{m_1})$. The **canonical reference section** $A_0 \in X_0$ is the normalized coordinate frame vector field:
$$
A_0(y) \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{m_1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y_i}}{\left\|\sum_{i=1}^{m_1}\frac{\partial}{\partial y_i}\right\|_{g(y)}}, \qquad \|A_0(y)\|_{g(y)} = 1 \;\implies\; \|A_0\|_{C_b^0} = 1
$$
grounding the tensor cascade strictly in the unit ball of continuous sections. The first syndrome section is generated by $f_1 \in \Oquant(r_1)$:
$$
A_1 \;\coloneqq\; f_1(A_0, \dots, A_0) \;\in\; X_1 \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_1}, T^{\otimes k_1}R_{m_1})
$$
:::

::: {.thm-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proposition 7.17 (Well-Typed Layered Cascade via Contravariant Musical Pullbacks):**
Let $X_\gamma \coloneqq \Gamma_b^0(R_{m_\gamma}, T^{\otimes k_\gamma}R_{m_\gamma})$ ($1 \le \gamma \le M$). Because contravariant tensors push forward rather than pull back directly along Riemannian submersions $\pi_\gamma \colon R_{m_\gamma} \to R_{m_{\gamma-1}}$ ($\|d\pi_\gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le 1$), define the **Contravariant Musical Pullback** $\pi_\gamma^\circledast$ via the metric musical isomorphisms $\flat_g \colon TR \xrightarrow{\sim} T^*R$ and $\sharp_g \colon T^*R \xrightarrow{\sim} TR$:
$$
\pi_\gamma^\circledast(A) \;\coloneqq\; \sharp_{g_{m_\gamma}}^{\otimes k_{\gamma-1}} \circ \pi_\gamma^* \circ \flat_{g_{m_{\gamma-1}}}^{\otimes k_{\gamma-1}}(A), \qquad \big\|\pi_\gamma^\circledast(A)\big\|_{C_b^0} \;\le\; \|A\|_{C_b^0}
$$
Then $X_0 \xrightarrow{f_1} X_1 \xrightarrow{f_2} \dots \xrightarrow{f_M} X_M$ is a strictly well-typed contractive cascade via $f_\gamma \circ (\pi_\gamma^\circledast)^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi r_\gamma} \colon X_{\gamma-1}^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi r_\gamma} \to X_\gamma$.
:::

## §7.3.3: Finite-Depth Cascade Norm Bound Theorem &amp; Induction Proof {.smaller auto-animate=true}

<div class="stratum-badge badge-b">STRATUM B: SCHOLIUM 7.18, THEOREM 7.19 &amp; COMPLETE INDUCTION PROOF | FORMALIZATION STAGE S₂ (LEAN 4)</div>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.thm-box}
**Scholium 7.18 &amp; Theorem 7.19 (Finite-Depth Layered Field Cascade Norm Estimate):**
Let $(X_\gamma)_{\gamma=0}^M$ be Banach spaces of bounded tensor sections and $f_\gamma \colon X_{\gamma-1}^{\widehat{\otimes}_\pi r_\gamma} \to X_\gamma$ be bounded multilinear operators with $\|f_\gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le C_\gamma < \infty$ ($\gamma = 1, \dots, M$). For $A_\gamma \coloneqq f_\gamma(A_{\gamma-1}, \dots, A_{\gamma-1})$, every stage $1 \le \gamma \le M$ satisfies the **monomial power bound**:
$$
\boxed{\|A_\gamma\|_{C_b^0} \;\le\; \Gamma_\gamma \, \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_\gamma}, \qquad D_\gamma \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^\gamma r_j, \qquad \Gamma_\gamma \coloneqq \prod_{j=1}^\gamma C_j^{\prod_{\ell=j+1}^\gamma r_\ell}}
$$
with $\Gamma_1 = C_1$. (*Safety mechanism preventing recursive metric fields from blowing up into unphysical singularities.*)
:::

::: {.proof-box .fragment .fade-up}
**Proof of Theorem 7.19 (Mathematical Induction on Cascade Depth $\gamma \ge 1$):**
1. **Base Case ($\gamma = 1$):** $A_1 = f_1(A_0, \dots, A_0) \implies \|A_1\|_{C_b^0} \le \|f_1\|_{\mathrm{op}}\prod_{i=1}^{r_1}\|A_0\|_{C_b^0} \le C_1 \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{r_1}$. Since $D_1 = r_1$ and $\Gamma_1 = C_1^{\prod_{\ell=2}^1 r_\ell} = C_1^1 = C_1$, the base case holds.
2. **Inductive Step ($\gamma - 1 \to \gamma$):** Assume $\|A_{\gamma-1}\|_{C_b^0} \le \Gamma_{\gamma-1}\|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_{\gamma-1}}$. Evaluating $A_\gamma = f_\gamma(A_{\gamma-1}, \dots, A_{\gamma-1})$:
   $$
   \|A_\gamma\|_{C_b^0} \le C_\gamma \|A_{\gamma-1}\|_{C_b^0}^{r_\gamma} \le C_\gamma \left(\Gamma_{\gamma-1}\|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{D_{\gamma-1}}\right)^{r_\gamma} = \left(C_\gamma \Gamma_{\gamma-1}^{r_\gamma}\right) \|A_0\|_{C_b^0}^{r_\gamma D_{\gamma-1}}
   $$
3. **Exponent &amp; Constant Aggregation:** $r_\gamma D_{\gamma-1} = \prod_{j=1}^\gamma r_j = D_\gamma$, and $C_\gamma \Gamma_{\gamma-1}^{r_\gamma} = C_\gamma \prod_{j=1}^{\gamma-1} C_j^{(\prod_{\ell=j+1}^{\gamma-1} r_\ell)r_\gamma} = \prod_{j=1}^\gamma C_j^{\prod_{\ell=j+1}^\gamma r_\ell} = \Gamma_\gamma$. $\blacksquare$
:::

<div class="lean-code-card fragment fade-right" style="margin-top:6px;">
<pre style="margin:0;"><code>theorem cascade_inductive_step (A_prev A_next C_g Γ_prev A0 : ℝ) (r_g D_prev : ℕ)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C_g) (hA : 0 ≤ A_prev) (h_ind : A_prev ≤ Γ_prev * A0 ^ D_prev)
    (h_op : A_next ≤ C_g * A_prev ^ r_g) :
    A_next ≤ (C_g * Γ_prev ^ r_g) * A0 ^ (D_prev * r_g) := by
  calc A_next ≤ C_g * (Γ_prev * A0 ^ D_prev) ^ r_g :=
         le_trans h_op (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (pow_le_pow_left hA h_ind r_g) hC)
       _ = (C_g * Γ_prev ^ r_g) * A0 ^ (D_prev * r_g) := by ring</code></pre>
</div>

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
